newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Aurora and Sidetrans to list on Bucharest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Aurora and Sidetrans to list on Bucharest bourse.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Monday two more companies would begin trading this week, bringing to 45 the total number of listed stocks.
A bourse statement said shares of footwear maker Aurora and transport company Sidertrans would start being traded on the exchange's second tier on Tuesday.
Aurora has a share capital of around 4.6 billion lei, in shares with a nominal value of 25,000 lei each. An employees' association holds 39.99 percent and the State Ownership Fund has 24.77 percent.
Individual stockholders, who got Aurora shares in exchange for privatisation paper in a mass selloff, have 35.23 percent and managers hold the rest.

The company posted a net profit of 1.9 billion lei last year, up from 244 million in 1995. Its future plans include investment in upgrading and promoting export-oriented production, the statement said. It paid 6,427 lei in net dividend per share in 1996, up from 384 lei the previous year.

Sidertrans has a share capital of some eight billion lei, in shares with a face value of 1,000 lei each. Mass selloff shareholders have 59.79 percent, the State Ownership Fund holds 39.95 percent and managers have the rest.
Sidertrans reported a net 1996 profit of 348 million lei, up from 218 million the previous year.
The company plans to extend its international freight transport in the future, the statement said.
The Bucharest bourse has seven listings on its first tier. ($=7,237 lei)
